title: A purge path for orphaned Workouts — and an orphaned `public` one stays readable after the account is gone
body:
## Problem

An athlete who deleted their account before #641 shipped (2026-10-25) left every Workout they wrote in the database as an ownerless row: titles, descriptions, notes, and for a published one the text that was shared with everyone. Since #641 the read path no longer serves these rows (`PUBLISHED_WORKOUT_WHERE` in `app/utils/community.ts`), and `deleteAccount` (`app/utils/account-deletion.server.ts`) purges an account's Workouts going forward. But the rows already orphaned are **still stored**. That breaks the promise the settings screen makes ("Kontoen, øktene og planene dine slettes for godt") and the retention table in ADR 0105. The former athlete cannot ask again because their account is gone.

A second gap lets the problem come back: nothing stops a future code path from calling `prisma.user.delete` directly. That path would create new orphans with nobody noticing. Today `deleteAccount` is the only delete path in `app/` and `server/` only by convention (ADR 0051 §5, "Deferred hardening"; #639 H25).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After the first deploy that carries this change, the orphaned Workouts already in the database are purged without an operator running anything: every athlete-authored Workout with no owner is erased, unless another athlete's session, Week Pattern slot or Program day points at it directly.
- [ ] An orphan that is kept because another athlete's training points at it ends up **withdrawn**, exactly as `deleteAccount` withdraws one: `private`, its Catalogue Entry retired, its Attribution deleted. That athlete's session, slot or Program day is still there and still opens with its Workout.
- [ ] Another athlete's fork of an erased orphan survives. Its `copiedFromId` now points at the nearest surviving ancestor, so a fork of an erased fork of a cited Stock Workout still shows its Citation. Where no ancestor survives it is `null`, and the fork still opens.
- [ ] An athlete who had bookmarked (`CatalogueSave`) an erased orphan opens their saved list and sees it without that row: no broken entry and no error.
- [ ] The purge touches no Stock Workout (`authorship = 'system'`, with or without a Catalogue Entry) and no Workout that has an owner. The Catalogue's stock and community tiers list the same rows before and after.
- [ ] The purge runs once: a later boot does not run it again. Running it again anyway changes nothing (an orphan already withdrawn stays withdrawn and is not erased).
- [ ] If the purge fails partway, nothing is half-erased (one transaction) and it is retried through the job queue's attempts.
- [ ] The purge records how many Workouts it erased, withdrew and spliced in the job's result or log. It records no Workout title, description or author name.
- [ ] Deleting an account through "Slett kontoen din" behaves as it does today (erase, withdraw where held elsewhere, splice), and both the purge and account deletion apply these rules from one implementation.
- [ ] Code in `app/` or `server/` that calls `user.delete` or `user.deleteMany` on a Prisma client outside account erasure fails `npm run lint`, and the error message names `deleteAccount`. Test files and test fixtures are exempt.
- [ ] ADR 0051 §5 "Deferred hardening" and ADR 0105's retention table say that pre-existing orphans are purged by this change and that lint pins the one deletion path. The read-only SQL count stays as the owner's check.

## Scope

In: a one-time purge of the athlete-authored Workouts that are already ownerless, using the same rules as `deleteAccount` (erase; withdraw where another athlete's training points at the row; splice the lineage of surviving forks). The rules move into one implementation that both share. Also in: a lint rule that keeps `deleteAccount` the only way a `User` is deleted, and the ADR updates that record both.

**Out of scope:**
- A recurring orphan sweep (decided below: lint prevents new orphans at the source).
- Keeping a de-identified tombstone of the moderation evidence on an erased Workout (#639 H24). Open reports on a purged orphan go with it, as they do on account deletion today.
- Custom Exercises an erased athlete authored (`Exercise.createdByAthleteId`, #639 H27).
- The profile image left in Tigris, and re-deleting accounts after a backup restore (ADR 0105, Deferred hardening).
- The read path, already closed by #641.

## What #448 changed

`Workout.ownerId` became nullable with `onDelete: SetNull` (previously `NOT NULL` / `Cascade`). ADR 0051 §2 is the reason: `SetNull` is what makes asserted `authorship` meaningful — an orphaned athlete-authored row reads *"author gone"* rather than *"trainm8 says so"*, and `Cascade` on a nullable `ownerId` would delete corpus content when one author leaves.

**Deleting an athlete now orphans their Workouts rather than deleting them.** ADR 0051:368-376 states this as the deliberate cost and says the purge is outstanding:

> A private Workout whose author is gone is unreachable through every owner-scoped query in the app, so nothing surfaces it — but a purge path for orphaned, non-Catalogue Workouts is genuine outstanding work rather than something this decision handles.

## Why it stopped being hidden

#452 shipped `public` visibility and a read path that is **not** owner-scoped — `listCatalogue` gained a `visibility: 'public'` arm. From #452's build report:

> ADR 0051's author-deleted-orphan purge now has a reachable case: an orphaned Workout that is still `public` stays readable after its author's account is deleted — correct as *attribution* (snapshotted), unexamined as *deletion policy*.

The Attribution display name is snapshotted on publish precisely so a join does not render an orphan as nobody (ADR 0052:127, :212). That is right for attribution and says nothing about whether the row should still be published.

## What is already decided and must not be re-litigated

The **retention rule** in ADR 0051 §5's sub-section already fixes a *different* orphan class — a preserved pre-edit Workout whose session is deleted, collected by #460 — and its four guards apply to any walk over this field. An unguarded walk deletes corpus content out from under every other athlete:

- **In the Catalogue → never.** A Catalogue Entry is retired, not deleted.
- **`authorship = 'system'` → never.** A **Stock Workout** is not the athlete's to collect.
- **Owned by someone else → never.**
- **Still referenced by anything → never** — another session, a Week Pattern slot, another fork, or anybody's list.

The shipped implementation of that walk is in `app/utils/workout.server.ts:388-406`, which counts `sessions`, `patternDays`, `copies` and `catalogueSaves` before taking a row. The author-deleted orphan is a **different case** — ADR 0051:374-376 says so explicitly — and is still outstanding.

## What a fix has to decide

- **There is no "delete my account" flow yet.** #452's report notes this. When one exists it has to decide whether it withdraws that athlete's published sessions, and that decision is upstream of any purge.
- Whether a purge is a policy on account deletion, a background sweep, or both.
- What a `public` orphan should become: stay published under the snapshotted Attribution, or be withdrawn to `private`. Withdrawing it strands nothing — `copiedFromId` is `SetNull` and forks keep resolving — but it removes content other athletes may have saved.

## Architecture

Follow [ADR 0112](``''''docs/adr/0112-orphaned-workouts-are-erased-once-by-a-boot-job-and-lint-keeps-deleteaccount-the-one-path.md''''``), ADR 0051 §5 "Account erasure" and ADR 0105 §3. Vocabulary: **Account Erasure** and **Orphaned Workout** (`GLOSSARY.md`). Read acceptance criterion 2's "withdrawn" as Account Erasure's **unattributed** keep: private, Catalogue Entry retired, Attribution deleted. It is not the author's withdrawal (`unpublishWorkout`), which keeps the Attribution. Do not reuse `unpublishWorkout` for it.

**1. One implementation, two entry points (restructure `app/utils/account-deletion.server.ts`).**
- Keep the rules private in this file: the held-elsewhere guard, keeping a row unattributed, the lineage splice capped at `MAX_LINEAGE_HOPS`, and the erase. Run them through one internal function over an erasure scope: `{ kind: 'account', userId }` or `{ kind: 'orphans' }`.
- Export `deleteAccount(userId)`, unchanged for callers, and `eraseOrphanedWorkouts(tx: Prisma.TransactionClient): Promise<AccountErasure>`. Both take the scope's candidate `where`:
  - account: `{ ownerId: userId }`
  - orphans: `{ ownerId: null, authorship: 'athlete' }`
- **Never thread `ownerId: null` through the current queries.** `deleteMany({ where: { ownerId: null, id: { notIn: kept } } })` erases every Stock Workout, and `copiedFrom: { ownerId: null }` reads every stock fork. The erase uses the candidate `where` (which carries `authorship`) plus `id notIn kept`. The splice selects children by `copiedFromId in <erasable ids>`, not by `copiedFrom.ownerId`.
- Held-elsewhere guard:
  - account scope: excludes the author's own sessions and Week Pattern slots, as today.
  - orphan scope: any session, any slot or any Program day keeps the row, because an orphan's author's training cascaded away with the account.
- `deleteAccount` keeps its own steps around the shared function: deleting the athlete's own Week Pattern slots first, then `tx.user.delete`, all in its one transaction with `TRANSACTION_OPTIONS`.
- Tests: one fixture set drives both entry points. Pin these:
  - a Stock Workout, with and without an entry, and its forks are untouched by the orphan scope;
  - an owned row is untouched;
  - a fork of an erased fork of a cited Stock Workout still resolves its Citation;
  - a `CatalogueSave` on an erased orphan disappears;
  - a second run changes nothing.

**2. The one-time job (new `app/utils/orphaned-workout-purge.server.ts`).**
- `ORPHANED_WORKOUT_PURGE_JOB_KIND`, `ensureOrphanedWorkoutPurgeEnqueued()` (any job row of the kind, in any state, means boot does not enqueue another; the `swim-pace-backfill.server.ts` shape) and `runOrphanedWorkoutPurge()`.
- Register the handler in `app/utils/jobs/handlers.server.ts`, and enqueue at boot in `server/index.ts` beside the other `ensure*Enqueued` calls.
- `runOrphanedWorkoutPurge` opens one `prisma.$transaction` with the same timeout. Inside it, it calls `eraseOrphanedWorkouts(tx)` and writes `{ erased, withdrawn, spliced }` onto its own running job row's `payload` in the same transaction, so a retry after a crash cannot lose or zero the record. After commit it logs the three counts. No title, description, display name or Workout id goes in the payload or the log.
- A failure throws, rolls back and is retried by the queue's attempts.

**3. Lint (`eslint.config.js`). This is a strained seam, settled by probe.**
- A second `no-restricted-syntax` block replaces the route files' native-`<select>` restriction rather than merging with it (evidence:lint-probes.txt).
- Hoist each restriction into a named constant. Add a block for `app/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and `server/**/*.ts` with the user-delete restriction. Its ignores: `app/utils/account-deletion.server.ts`, `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` and the fixture paths. Make the route-file block list **both** restrictions.
- Selector, probed against `prisma.user.delete`, `tx.user.deleteMany` and a batch `$transaction([...])`, and silent on `userImage`/`session`: `CallExpression[callee.type='MemberExpression'][callee.property.name=/^(delete|deleteMany)$/][callee.object.type='MemberExpression'][callee.object.property.name='user']`
- The message names `deleteAccount` and says why: `Workout.ownerId` is `SetNull`, so a bare delete leaves Orphaned Workouts.
- Add a vitest that lints a snippet through the ESLint API at a route path and at a `app/utils` path. It asserts both restrictions fire where they apply, so neither can shadow the other again.

**4. Docs.** ADR 0112, the glossary entries, and the ADR 0051 §5 Deferred hardening and ADR 0105 §3 updates (acceptance criterion 11) are already committed on this branch. If the build changes a name above (module, job kind, export), update ADR 0112 to match.

## Decisions

- **What happens to orphans that already exist** (spec): Apply the deleteAccount policy. Erase every athlete-authored ownerless Workout, published ones and ones with open reports included. Withdraw (private, entry retired, Attribution deleted) only those another athlete's session, Week Pattern slot or Program day points at directly., because The owner confirmed this policy for account deletion on 2026-10-25 (ADR 0051 §5): withdrawal keeps the athlete's text with no reader and no purpose. A row orphaned before #641 is the same row from the same act, so it gets the same treatment. Rejected: Withdraw every orphan to private: keeps a deleted athlete's text forever, against the settings copy and ADR 0105. Keep reported orphans until the H24 tombstone exists: holds a gone author's content on an unscheduled ticket.. One-way door: the ownerless Workout rows already stored in production. Decided by the factory (autonomy `full`).
- **How the purge reaches production** (spec): A one-time job enqueued at boot, with the job row as its marker (the `ensure*Enqueued` pattern in `server/index.ts`, e.g. `swim-pace-backfill.server.ts`). The job calls the erasure rules extracted from `deleteAccount` into one TypeScript implementation that both use., because The rules (the held-elsewhere guard, withdrawal, an in-memory lineage splice capped at MAX_LINEAGE_HOPS) already exist in tested TypeScript. A second copy in SQL would be a recursive CTE that nothing typechecks, and it would drift from deleteAccount. That is ADR 0051 §9's reason for not shipping logic-bearing data in a migration. It still needs no operator, and the job queue gives it retries. Rejected: A guarded SQL migration, as the ADR's Deferred hardening note suggested: it duplicates the splice and withdraw logic in SQL that cannot be unit-tested against the same fixtures as deleteAccount.. One-way door: erasure rules live in one module shared by account deletion and the purge. Decided by the factory (autonomy `full`).
- **How to keep new orphans from appearing** (spec): Add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule on `user.delete` / `user.deleteMany` calls in `app/` and `server/`. It exempts `account-deletion.server.ts`, test files and test fixtures, and its message points at `deleteAccount`. Add no recurring sweep., because Lint stops the cause at the call site, at review time. A recurring sweep would quietly clean up after a regression instead of catching it. It would also contradict ADR 0051 §5 ("a policy on account deletion, not a sweep"), and the retention sweep it would sit beside (ADR 0105) is not built. Rejected: A daily orphan sweep: hides the regression it cleans up after. A test that greps the source: reports the problem later than lint and farther from the line that caused it.. Two-way door.
- **Where the shared erasure rules live and how the purge selects orphans** (architecture): One private function in account-deletion.server.ts over an erasure scope (account | orphans), exported as deleteAccount(userId) and eraseOrphanedWorkouts(tx); orphans selected by authorship = 'athlete' AND ownerId IS NULL; splice by copiedFromId in the erasable ids, because Keeps the rules in one place for both callers. The scope carries authorship, so the corpus cannot be reached by accident. Rejected: Threading a nullable userId through the existing queries, where ownerId: null in the final deleteMany erases every Stock Workout. Also a separate purge module that copies the rules.. Two-way door.
- **Where the purge records its counts** (architecture): On its own Job.payload inside the purge transaction, then a log line after commit; counts only, because The record commits with the rows it describes, so a retry after a crash cannot lose it or overwrite it with zeros. This follows the swim-pace backfill's audit shape. Rejected: Writing the payload after the purge commits, which leaves a crash window. Logging only, which is lost with the log retention.. Two-way door.
- **How the user-delete lint rule coexists with the route files' <select> restriction** (architecture): Named restriction constants composed in eslint.config.js (route block lists both), plus a vitest that lints snippets at a route and a utils path, because Flat config replaces no-restricted-syntax options per block (probed), so a separate block would silently drop the existing guard. Rejected: A separate block, which shadows the existing guard. A local ESLint plugin rule, which is more machinery for one selector.. Two-way door.
- **Supersede ADR 0051's guarded-cleanup-migration note with ADR 0112** (architecture): New ADR 0112 records the boot job and the lint pin; ADR 0051 §5 Deferred hardening and ADR 0105 §3 point at it, because The spec chose a boot job over the migration ADR 0051 suggested. The ADRs must say what production now does, and AC 11 asks for this. Rejected: Amending ADR 0051 in place with the full rationale (workspace rule: a new ADR file, not an addendum). One-way door: ADR 0051 §5's plan for pre-existing orphans. Decided by the factory (autonomy `full`).
- **Name the row Account Erasure keeps 'unattributed', not 'withdrawn'** (architecture): Add Account Erasure and Orphaned Workout to GLOSSARY.md; the kept row is unattributed, because The glossary's withdrawal is the author's reversible act and keeps the Attribution. Erasure deletes it. The shared word would lead a builder to reuse unpublishWorkout. Rejected: Keep 'withdrawn' as ADR 0051 §5 uses it, which contradicts the Shared Workout and Attribution entries. Two-way door.
- **A purge run after one that committed keeps the first record** (implement): runOrphanedWorkoutPurge writes payload.purged only when it is absent; a later run (worker crashed after commit, before marking the job done) leaves the first counts in place, because The second run finds nothing to erase, so writing its counts would overwrite the real record with zeros, which ADR 0112 §2 says must not happen. Rejected: Always overwrite with the latest run's counts, which zeroes the audit after a crash between commit and completion. Two-way door.
- **Route test files keep the native-<select> guard under the composed lint config** (implement): A third eslint block applies only NATIVE_SELECT_RESTRICTION to app/routes/**/*.test.tsx, since the route block now ignores test files for the user-delete exemption, because The guard keeps covering exactly the files it covered before, and test files stay exempt from the user-delete rule as the issue asks. Rejected: Exempting route tests from both restrictions, which quietly narrows the existing guard; or applying user-delete to route tests, against AC 10. Two-way door.
- **Name the purge record's kept count keptUnattributed** (review): `{ erased, keptUnattributed, spliced }` in the erasure result and the job payload; ADR 0112 §2 says so, because GLOSSARY.md (Account Erasure) lists 'withdrawn' under Avoid for the kept row; the architecture's literal `withdrawn` key contradicted the glossary decision made in the same issue, and nothing in production has read the payload yet. Rejected: keep `withdrawn` with a doc comment, which leaves the audit record reading as the author's withdrawal. Two-way door.
- **The job retention sweep keeps one-time job rows** (review): ADR 0112 Consequences: when ADR 0105's proposed 30-day job-row retention is built, it keeps the orphaned-workout-purge row (run-once marker and record), because deleting the row would re-enqueue the purge on the next boot and lose the counts the issue chose to keep on the job rather than in logs. Rejected: move the marker and record to a dedicated table now, which builds machinery for a sweep that does not exist. Two-way door.

comments.body:
**Triage (2026-10-24): `ready-for-human`.** Still valid, and more urgent than when it was filed: account deletion now exists (`settings/profile/index.tsx:783-784`, `prisma.user.delete`). `Workout.ownerId` is `onDelete: SetNull`, and the catalogue's public arm (`catalogue.server.ts:89-93`) doesn't exclude orphans. So an orphaned public Workout can happen today. The owner must decide whether deleting an account withdraws its published Workouts.
